en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-dīrghāyur-aparādhakṣaya-sarvakiśorarakṣā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by the Śramaṇa Buddhāpāli of Kaśmīr by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus.
The assembly consisted of one thousand two hundred and fifty people, together with twelve thousand great bodhisattvas, as well as devas, nāgas,
and the eight classes of spirits— humans and non-humans— all gathered together for the preaching of the Dharma.
At that time, from the gateway of his face, the World-Honored One, by means of the Buddha’s supernatural power, emitted various kinds of light.
These lights were of five colors—blue, yellow, red, and white—and within each single color were immeasurable transformation Buddhas capable of performing the work of a Buddha in inconceivable ways.
Each of these transformation Buddhas had immeasurable transformation Bodhisattvas who praised the virtues of the Buddha. Those lights were subtle and wondrous. Difficult...

It can be measured: reaching upward to the Heaven of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception and downward to the Avīci Hell, it completely encompasses eighty thousand [yojanas], leaving no place unilluminated.
Among the sentient beings therein, those who encounter the Buddha’s light spontaneously recollect the Buddha and all attain the Expedient Samādhi of the First Stage (*prathamabhūmi*).
At that time, within the assembly, there were forty-nine bodhisattvas who had newly resolved their minds, each desiring to follow [the Buddha].
The Buddha sought long life, yet none dared to pose a question.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, knowing there were those harboring doubts, rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One, I see that there are those among the assembly who have doubts and now wish to inquire. I only pray that the Tathāgata will grant me leave to speak. The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent, Mañjuśrī! Whatever you have doubts about, you should feel free to ask.
Mañjuśrī said, "World-Honored One, all sentient beings within the ocean of birth and death create various evil karmas; from kalpa to kalpa, they transmigrate through the six realms.
Even if they obtain a human body, they receive the retribution of a short life. How can one cause them to obtain a long life and extinguish [these evils]?"
"Regarding all these evil karmas, we only pray that the World-Honored One will expound the Dharma of Longevity. The Buddha said, "Mañjuśrī, your great compassion is immeasurable;

you take pity on sentient beings suffering from their transgressions and are able to ask about this matter. However, if I were to explain it in full detail, no sentient beings would be able to believe and accept it.
Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha again, saying, "World-Honored One, you possess the knowledge of all modes and are the Teacher of Gods and Humans."
He universally covers all sentient beings; he is the Great Compassionate Father. With a single voice he expounds the Dharma; he is the Great Dharma King.

I only pray that the World-Honored One will take pity on us and explain this extensively. The Buddha then smiled and addressed the great assembly: "Listen attentively, all of you! I shall now speak for your sake."
In a past age, there was a world named Vimalaviśuddha.

In that land there was a Buddha, titled Samantaprabhā-samyagdṛṣṭi Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.
He was revered by an immeasurable and boundless assembly of bodhisattvas.
Surrounding him, within that Buddha’s teaching, there was a female lay follower named Viparyāsa (Inversion). Hearing that a Buddha had appeared in the world, she sought to leave the household life.
Wailing and weeping piteously, she addressed that Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, I possess evil karma and seek to repent it.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant me permission to speak fully. In the past, my body was pregnant for a full eight months..."
Because of the family law, Yue did not desire [to have] children; she consequently took poison and killed her child, injuring the fetus.
Only the dead child remained, its human form complete. I once heard a wise person come and say to me:

"If you persist in injuring the fetus, this person shall receive the retribution of a grave illness in the present life, with a short and meager lifespan, and fall into the Avīci Hell to undergo great suffering and distress. I now only...

Reflecting thus, he was struck with great compassion and fear, and prayed: "I only beseech the World-Honored One to use the power of your compassion to preach the Dharma for me, grant me permission to leave the household life, and enable me to escape this suffering."
At that time, the Tathāgata Samantaprabha-samyagdṛṣṭi addressed Viparyāsa, saying: "In the world, there are five kinds of repentance that are difficult to extinguish.
What are these five? First, killing one's father; second, killing one's mother; third, killing an embryo;
fourth, shedding the blood of a Buddha; and fifth, causing a schism in the Saṃgha. Such evil karma makes it difficult for the transgression to be extinguished. At that time, Viparyāsa...

She overturned the woman’s [image], wailing and sobbing with a choked voice, weeping bitterly with tears falling like rain. Prostrating herself with her five limbs touching the ground, she rolled about before the Buddha and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One, you of great compassion who protect all beings, I only pray that the World-Honored One will take pity on me and preach the Dharma.
The Tathāgata Samantaprabhā-samyagdṛṣṭi then spoke again, saying: “This evil karma of yours shall cause you to fall into the Avīci Hell; there is no [escape].”
There is respite: in the hot hells, one may briefly encounter a cold wind, and the sinner is briefly cooled; in the cold hells, one may briefly encounter a hot wind, and the sinner is briefly warmed.
However, in the Avīci Hell, there is no such place. The fire from above penetrates below, and the fire from below penetrates above;
iron walls surround it on all four sides, with iron nets fixed upon them, and at the four gates—east, west, north, and south—there is fierce karmic fire. If...
There is one person whose body also fills the entire hell; his body is eighty thousand *yojanas* tall. If there are many people, they likewise fill it entirely.
Over the bodies of these sinners, there are great iron snakes whose venomous agony is more intense than a fierce fire.

Sometimes entering through the mouth, they emerge from the eyes or ears, coiling all around the body from kalpa to kalpa. From the limbs and joints of the sinners, a fierce [flame] constantly issues forth.
There is fire. Furthermore, there are iron crows that peck at and eat their flesh; or there are copper dogs that gnaw upon their bodies.

The ox-headed hell-wardens hold weapons in their hands and let out a great, evil sound like the crash of thunder and lightning. "Because you stubbornly killed a fetus, you must undergo this suffering.
If I were to speak falsely, I would not be called a Buddha. At that time, the woman who had been deluded, having heard the Buddha’s words, was filled with grief.

He fell prostrate on the ground and gradually regained his breath. He addressed the Buddha again, saying: "World-Honored One, am I alone who undergoes this agony, or do all sentient beings likewise suffer this pain?"
The Tathāgata Samantaprabha addressed the Perversion, saying: "Your child is in the womb, possessing a complete human form.

Within the two receptacles—the raw and the cooked—it is like being in hell, with two stones pressing upon its body. When the mother eats hot food, it is like a hot hell; when the mother eats cold food, it is like a cold hell.
It suffers pain throughout the day, dwelling in ignorance. You, moreover, harbor an evil heart and persistently consume poison."
"Medicine! As for this evil karma of yours, you shall fall into Avīci Hell yourself; the sinners there will be your companions.

The woman, distraught and wailing piteously, spoke again: 'I have heard the wise say that if one commits various evils but encounters the Buddha and the Sangha, those sins are extinguished through repentance.
Even if, at the end of life, one enters the various hells, one who has performed even small merits will still be able to be reborn.'"
"O Deva, what do you think? Please explain this for me.
Thus addressed, the Tathāgata Samantaprabhāsasamyagdṛṣṭi spoke to Viparyāsa:

"If there are sentient beings who have committed various grave offenses, yet encounter the Buddha and the Saṅgha and repent with utmost sincerity, vowing not to commit them again, their sins shall be extinguished. Even if they should reach the end of their lives, Yama..."

While the Dharma King Loka was deliberating and had not yet reached a decision, the living six kinds of relatives and kin of the deceased invited the Buddha and the Saṃgha to recite the Mahāyāna Vaipulya sūtras for seven days, burning incense and scattering flowers.
At that time, the messengers of the underworld would come to investigate and verify their good and evil deeds;
carrying divine banners of five colors, they would arrive at the place of the King, with songs of praise and hymns of eulogy preceding and following the banners.
He uttered a subtle and wondrous voice, gentle, harmonious, and compliant, and replied to King Yama: "This person has accumulated merit.

Or perhaps there are many deceased who, within seven days, believed in heterodox and perverted views, did not believe in the Buddha-dharma or the Mahāyāna sūtras, and lacked filial piety and compassion."
Lacking a compassionate heart, the messengers of the underworld arrive, carrying a black banner. Before and behind this banner are immeasurable evil spirits, who report to King Yama:
"This person has accumulated evil. At that time, King Yama, the Dharma King, sees the five-colored banners approaching.
His heart was filled with great joy, and he cried out in a loud voice: "May this sinful body of mine also become as virtuous as yours!
At that moment, the various hells were transformed into clear springs, and the mountains of knives and trees of swords became like blooming lotuses; all the sinners—
All shall receive happiness. If one sees a black banner, King Yama will become enraged;

with a terrifying roar that shatters all, he will then consign the sinner to the eighteen hells—either up the sword-tree, or into the mountain of knives, or upon the iron bed, or embracing the copper pillar.
They are ploughed with oxen and have their tongues pulled out; they are pounded by pestles and ground by millstones. Within a single day, they die ten thousand times and are born ten thousand times.
Thus they continue in succession until they fall into the Avīci Hell, where they undergo great agony from kalpa to kalpa without any respite. Before he had finished speaking, [the beings were seen].
At that time, a great and terrible voice arose from the air, crying out: "Inverted woman! You have stubbornly killed your fetus; you shall receive the retribution of a short life.
I am a messenger of the hells, come here specifically to pursue you. The inverted woman was struck with terror and wept piteously as she clasped the feet of the Tathāgata, saying:
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will extensively explain for me the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas and the causes and conditions for extinguishing sin, so that upon death I may—"
The vow was completed.
At that time, the Tathāgata Universal Radiance Right View, by the power of a Buddha, replied to the ghost-messenger:
"O Unconstant Killing Ghost, I now wish to preach for the woman of inverted views the Sūtra on Long Life and the Extinction of Sin. Wait but a moment. From this—

There shall be realization. Listen attentively! I shall, for your sake, expound the *Sūtra of the Longevity of the Secret Dharma of All Buddhas*, based upon the thousand Buddhas of the past, so as to cause you all to remain far removed from the evil realms.

You should understand that this ghost of impermanence and death is difficult to escape even with a longing desire, regardless of whether one possesses immeasurable hundreds or thousands of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, tridacna shell, or red pearls.
Even if one attempts to ransom their life with agate, they cannot escape.

Even if kings, princes, ministers, or elders rely upon their power and influence, when the ghost of impermanence arrives, it severs their precious lives; not a single person can escape. You should understand this inversion of reality.
Only the single word "Buddha" can deliver one from this suffering. There are two kinds of people in the world who are exceedingly rare, as difficult to encounter as the udumbara flower:
first, those who do not commit unwholesome deeds; second, those who are able to repent immediately upon committing a transgression.

Such a person is truly rare. Since you are able to repent before me with a sincere heart, I shall recite the *Āyuṣmat-sūtra* for you, so that you may be freed from the suffering of the ghosts of impermanence.
You must understand this correctly: in future ages, such people will be exceedingly rare.
In this age of the five turbidities, if there are sentient beings who commit various grave offenses— such as killing their father, harming their mother,

using poison to kill a fetus, destroying stupas, ruining monasteries, shedding the blood of a Buddha, or causing a schism in the harmonious Sangha— these are sentient beings who have committed the five heinous crimes.

If one can receive and uphold this *Āyuṣmat-sūtra*, transcribing, reading, and reciting it—whether transcribing it oneself or commissioning another to do so—one’s sins will be extinguished and one shall attain rebirth in the Brahma Heaven;
how much more so for you now, who have personally seen me. Well done, Upāli!
For immeasurable and vast eons, you have planted various roots of goodness. Because of your excellent questioning and your earnest repentance, I am now [gratified].
I have attained the ability to turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma; I am able to cross the boundless great ocean of birth and death;
I am able to wage war against Pāpīyān; and I am able to topple the victorious banner established by Pāpīyān. Listen attentively: I shall now rely upon the Buddhas of the past.
He taught the Dharma of the twelve links of dependent origination:

ignorance conditions volitional formations; volitional formations condition consciousness; consciousness conditions name-and-form; name-and-form conditions the six sense bases; the six sense bases condition contact.

Contact conditions feeling; feeling conditions craving; craving conditions clinging; clinging conditions existence; existence conditions birth; birth conditions aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and despair.
With the cessation of ignorance, volitional formations cease; with the cessation of volitional formations, consciousness ceases; with the cessation of consciousness, name-and-form ceases.

With the cessation of name-and-form, the six sense bases cease. With the cessation of the six sense bases, contact ceases. With the cessation of contact, feeling ceases. With the cessation of feeling, craving ceases.
With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases. With the cessation of clinging, existence ceases. With the cessation of existence, birth ceases.
With the cessation of birth, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, and despair cease. One should know that all sentient beings, due to their inverted views, are unable to see this.
The twelve links of dependent origination are that by which one revolves through the miserable realms of birth and death.

If there is anyone who perceives these twelve links of dependent origination, they perceive the Dharma; he who perceives the Dharma perceives the Buddha; and he who perceives the Buddha perceives the Buddha-nature.
Why is this? Because all Buddhas take this as their nature. You have now heard me explain these twelve links of dependent origination.
Because you have now attained the purity of the Buddha-nature and are a fit vessel for the Dharma, I shall explain to you the Single True Path.
You should contemplate it and guard a single thought-moment. A single thought-moment refers to the bodhicitta; as for this bodhicitta:
It is called the Great Vehicle. For the sake of sentient beings, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have provisionally taught three [vehicles].
You should, in every thought-moment, constantly and diligently protect this bodhicitta so that it is never forgotten or lost.

Even if the five aggregates, the four snakes, the three poisons, the six thieves, or all manner of māras should come to harass you, they will ultimately be unable to alter this bodhicitta. By means of this, you shall attain...
Because of such bodhicitta, the body is like a vajra and the mind is like space, being difficult to destroy or corrupt.
Because it is indestructible, one immediately attains anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Because one attains anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, the qualities of permanence, bliss, self, and purity are fully possessed. Thus, one is able to remain far removed from this impermanence.
"The ghosts of slaughter, birth, old age, sickness, death, and the various hells sufferings.
When the Buddha preached this Dharma among the great assembly, the ghost-messenger from empty space spoke these words:
"I have heard, World-Honored One, that you have preached this essential Dharma; the hells have become purified and transformed into lotus ponds. I now renounce my realm as a ghost for the present."
The ghost replied again, "Inverted One, when you attain the Way, I pray that you will deliver me.
At that time, the Tathāgata Samantaprabhā-samyagdṛṣṭi further addressed the Inverted One: "I have already finished explaining the twelve links of dependent origination for you;
I shall further explain the six pāramitās for you. You should receive and uphold them: the Prajñāpāramitā and Dhyāna..."
The perfection of vigor, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline,
and the perfection of generosity— these six perfections you should receive and uphold.
Furthermore, I shall now recite for you the verses concerning the attainment of Buddhahood by the Buddhas of the past.
He spoke these verses: "All conditioned phenomena are impermanent; They are of the nature of arising and ceasing. When arising and ceasing have ceased, Cessation is bliss.
At that time, the woman who had been deluded heard the Dharma with joy; her mind became suddenly clear and pure, and she attained clear and thorough awakening through the Buddha’s [teaching].
By means of his supernormal power, he ascended into the air to a height of seven *tāla* trees and sat there in meditative composure.
At that time, there was a brahmin of great lineage whose family was immensely wealthy, with no one able to equal them; he suddenly fell gravely ill, and physicians attended to him.
"A person's eyes are needed to compound a medicine for a cure. At that time, the great householder immediately ordered his servants to go out into the streets and proclaim in a loud voice:
"Who can bear the pain of selling a pair of eyes? I shall give them a thousand pieces of gold and the precious treasures from my storehouses."
Whatever was required, he never begrudged it. Upon hearing these words, the perverse woman was filled with great joy and thought to herself:
"I have now heard the *Longevity Sūtra* from the Buddha; my evil karma has been extinguished, and my mind is now clearly enlightened."
I have awakened to the nature of all Buddhas and attained liberation from the suffering of the various hells caused by the demon of impermanence that slays.

I shall now shatter my own body to repay the compassionate grace of the Buddha. He cried out in a loud voice: "This year I have reached the age of forty-nine; it is from the Buddha that I have heard the Dharma."

This is called the *Āyuṣmat-sūtra*. Now, wishing to crush my body and not sparing my life, I shall transcribe the *Āyuṣmat-sūtra* in forty-nine fascicles, so that all sentient beings may receive, uphold, read, and recite it. To do this, I must sell my eyes;
my eyes are priceless, so give me whatever price you will. At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, transformed himself into forty-nine people and went to where the man was lying on his back.
"I vow to act as your scribe for this sutra so that, having seen it, you may sell your eyes at will. At that time, the woman Paryasta rejoiced immeasurably;
she pared her own bones to make pens, tore the flesh from her body, and used her blood as ink to provide for the scribe.

Within seven days, they finished copying the sutra. Once everyone had completed their writing, they said to Viparyāsa, "Regarding the two eyes you previously promised us for our labor, we have now finished our work;
please hand them over so that we may sell them to a Brahmin.
At that time, Viparyāsa immediately commanded a Caṇḍāla, "You must gouge out my eyes for me; let forty..."
"Nine people shall divide one portion for you. At that time, as the *caṇḍāla* was about to gouge her according to the law, forty-nine people chanted in unison:
"Rare! Rare! Inconceivable! This perverse woman endures the filth of this wound even as her bones are scraped and blood flows;
she does not spare her own body or life to transcribe this sutra. How could we take her eyes? Out of compassion..."
The Heart addressed the woman with inverted views, saying: "We shall never covet your eyes, O Brahmin-seller.

May you attain the Way; we pray that you shall deliver us. We only wish that in every place and at every future birth, we may always be together with you, acting as spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) to proclaim this sutra and rescue all beings from their sins and suffering."

Sentient beings, at that time, Nanda the Dragon King and others, by means of great supernatural power, performed various illusory arts to steal the Perverted Sūtras and received, upheld, and made offerings to them within the dragon palace.
Then, in a mere instant, the Perverted Woman suddenly found the sūtras missing. They flowed away...

With tears and a choked voice, he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, I had ground my own body to write out the *Longevity Sūtra*, desiring to cause it to be circulated among all sentient beings.
Now, suddenly, I do not know where it has gone. My heart is clouded with distress; my grief and bitterness are unbearable."
The Tathāgata Samantaprabha addressed Viparyāsa, saying: "Your sūtra has been requested by the eight classes of dragon kings to remain within their palaces;
you shall uphold and make offerings to it. You should rejoice; there is no need for sorrow or distress. Excellent, Viparyāsa!
By the power of these merits, at the end of this life, you shall be reborn in the heavens of the Formless Realm (ārūpyadhātu) and experience all manner of happiness, never again [to suffer]."
Having taken the body of a woman, that woman, who was then in a state of delusion, addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, as for my aspiration, I do not wish to be born in the heavens;

I only pray that in birth after birth and from age to age, I may always encounter the World-Honored One, whose resolve never regresses, and that wherever he may be, he will always proclaim this Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings suffering from the retribution of their sins."
Samantaprabha said, "You should speak falsely. Viparyāsa replied, "If I speak falsely, may I be oppressed by the same impermanent ghosts as before;
if I speak with a sincere heart, may the sores on my body be healed in the presence of the Buddha. At that time, Viparyāsa—
By the power of his vow, [the land] was restored to its former state. The Tathāgata Samantaprabha addressed Viparyasta, saying: "Recite the Buddha's name with single-minded devotion;
from one buddha-field to another buddha-field, you shall be able to see immeasurable and boundless worlds of the Buddhas, whose names and words cannot be fully described.
At that moment, in an instant, Viparyasta attained the realization of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
The patience regarding dharmas and the mind of *samyaksambodhi*.
Mañjuśrī, you should know that the Tathāgata Samantaprabha was my own self, and the woman who was perverted was your own self.
These forty-nine people are bodhisattvas who have newly resolved their minds.

Since immeasurable and vast kalpas past, I have constantly protected them with my own body and have always expounded this sutra for you all, so that all sentient beings may eliminate every evil karma.
"Having heard even half a verse of this *Sūtra of Longevity* with one's ears, all [sins] are extinguished. Now it shall be spoken once more.
At that time, during the night, King Prasenajit was within his royal palace when he heard a woman wailing loudly, her lamentation so unbearable that she could not overcome her grief.
He thought to himself, "In my inner palace, there has never before been..."
"Regarding this matter, for what reason is there this voice of such piteous distress?

At the break of dawn, he immediately commanded his officials to go to the city streets and seek out this woman, instructing them to obey the King’s decree and bring her back. The woman was struck with terror and fell into a swoon before the King.
The King sprinkled cold water upon her face, and she gradually regained consciousness. The Great King asked: 'Last night...'"
She wept and cried out. "Is this truly you? she asked. The woman replied, "It is I who am grieving. The king said, "For what reason do you cry in resentment? Who has wronged you?
The woman replied, "That which I resent is not actually caused by anyone else. I only pray that Your Majesty [will grant me my wish]."
Listen to what I say: I was fourteen years old when I first went to my husband’s home. Thirty years have passed since then, and I have borne thirty sons.
Their countenances are exceptionally beautiful; their hair is a deep azure-blue, their lips are red as vermilion, their teeth are white as jade, and their bodies are full of vitality.
Like flowers in springtime, my affection for him was like that for my very marrow and brain, as well as my liver and entrails; it was dearer to me than life itself.
This son had not yet reached the age of one year when, during the autumn or summer, he abandoned me and died. He was my youngest child.
"He is truly my life. Now he is on the verge of exhaustion; his life is about to end. Last night I wept aloud, and it was because of this sorrow.
When the Great King heard these words, he was deeply and greatly distressed. "All the common people depend upon me."
"If one does not provide protection, one cannot be called a king. He then assembled his ministers to deliberate together. The king had six ministers:
the first was named Vision of Form, the second Hearing of Sound, the third Fragrant Feet, the fourth Eloquence, and the fifth Following Conditions.

The sixth was named Yiran (Easy-to-Infect). He spoke to the King, saying: "When the prince was first born, a ritual altar for the seven stars and the twenty-eight lunar mansions should have been established to extend his life;
only then could he have avoided this suffering. I pray that Your Majesty will issue a decree throughout the land.

At that time, there was a wise minister named Dinghui (Samādhi-Prajñā), who had planted various roots of goodness under immeasurable Buddhas in the past. He stepped forward and addressed the Great King.
"Great King, you should know that what the six ministers have said cannot truly exempt one from suffering. Now there is a Great Master named Gautama, titled Siddhārtha;
having attained self-awakening without a teacher, he has now become a Buddha. He is currently at Vulture Peak Mountain preaching the *Āyuṣmat-sūtra*.
I only pray that the Great King will go there to hear and receive it. If even half a verse of this sūtra enters one’s ears, for hundreds of kalpas and thousands..."

All grave sins will be extinguished without exception. All children who hear this sutra with their ears, though they have not yet attained understanding, shall naturally attain long life through the merit of the sutra.
King Prasenajit said: "In the past, I heard what the six teachers said:
'The śramaṇa Gautama has studied for but a short time; he is a yellow-faced child of tender years. Regarding the sutras of the six teachers—"
"Among these, Gautama is one who specializes in the illusory transformations of portents and omens. Those who revere him mostly lose the true path.
At that time, Dinghui addressed the king with a verse:
Śākyamuni, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Having practiced austerities for immeasurable eons, you have now attained Buddhahood and turned the wheel of Dharma.
You preach in accordance with the teachings of all past Buddhas, Never failing to fulfill the vows of all sentient beings;
With great compassion and mighty power, you rescue the deluded masses.
"Seeing the Buddha is like a tortoise encountering a floating log, Or like the most wondrous *udumbara* flower.
I only pray that Your Majesty will go to hear the Dharma, And not believe the words of the six heretical teachers.
At that time, Dinghui (Dhyānaprajñā), having spoken this verse, used his supernormal powers to leap up from the ground and ascend into the void.
Standing seven *tāla* trees tall, he performed various incantations before the king.

In a single moment, he caused Mount Sumeru and the waters of the great ocean to enter his heart, remaining there peacefully and without obstruction. Upon witnessing this, King Prasenajit exclaimed in admiration, "How extraordinary!
You are a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*). He then prostrated before Samādhiprajñā and said to her, "This is your teacher."
“Who? Jñānagupta replied, “My teacher is Śākyamuni Buddha.
He is currently at Vulture Peak Mountain in the great city of Rājagṛha, preaching the *Āyuḥpramāṇa-pāpavināśana-sūtra*. Upon hearing these words, the King was filled with great joy.
He immediately entrusted the affairs of state to Jñānagupta for a time and, accompanied by immeasurable retinues, ministers, elders, and horse-drawn jeweled chariots, proceeded forward.
Surrounded by his retinue, together with this woman and the youth, carrying flower garlands and making hundreds of kinds of offerings, he arrived at Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain in Rājagṛha.
Having removed all his finery, he circumambulated the Buddha seven times, joined his palms, and prostrated himself in worship.
She scattered flowers as an offering and, having completed all the aforementioned rites, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"At that time, the World-Honored One, told King Prasenajit: 'This woman, in a past life, was a stepmother.
Out of a heart of jealousy, she prepared a toxic potion and killed thirty children—the sons of her predecessor’s wife. These children..."
They were killed. Each of them made a vow, saying: "May I, in birth after birth throughout all lifetimes, always become his son.
Thereupon they parted, causing her such bitter anguish that she gave rise to great sorrow. Now, this woman has come to hear a single verse from my *Dīrghāyuṣya-sūtra* reach her ears;
from this moment forth, her enemies and creditors shall be forever severed.

At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly: "When a youth is conceived in the womb, Māra Pāpīyān immediately releases the four great venomous serpents and the evil bandits of the six sense-objects to dwell within his body. If even one of these is not subdued, his life-force will be severed.
I possess a dhāraṇī mantra that is well able to increase the lifespan of all youths. If there is any suffering or affliction, upon hearing this mantra of mine," [the illness shall be cured].
Once it passes through the ear, there is nothing that is not cured. It can cause evil spirits to scatter and flee in all directions. Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

Lì wén zhèi chēn dié pín dié bān shì mò dié chí nà jiā lí sū pó hē.
Buddha said: These are the phrases of the dhāraṇī mantra. If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives, maintains, reads, and recites them...
It is for the sake of all children who suffer from the ailments of conception and birth that this is expounded.

For seven days and seven nights, one should burn incense, scatter flowers, transcribe [the text], make offerings, and listen with a sincere heart. All grave illnesses and karmic obstacles from previous lives will be completely extinguished.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Jīvaka, the King of Physicians, came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, I am a great physician who treats all manner of illnesses.
There are nine kinds of diseases among young children that can shorten their lives. What are these nine?"
First, the parents engage in sexual intercourse at an improper time. Second, they cause the ground to become defiled by blood upon the first birth;

thus the Earth Deity does not dwell there, and malevolent spirits find an opportunity. Third, they do not remove the various small venomous insects from between the umbilical cord after the first birth.
Fourth, they do not wipe away the impure blood from within the womb with soft *tūla* cotton. Fifth, they kill living beings and take their lives. And so forth...
Sixth, his mother consumed various kinds of cold fruits. Seventh, when the boy was ill, she fed him various kinds of meat.

Eighth, at the time of birth, while the mother and child were not yet separated, inauspicious influences arose. Those who see the place of birth before the separation is complete can cause the mother’s death;
once the separation is complete, they cause the boy’s death. What are these inauspicious influences? If...
There are those who see all corpses and various portents with their own eyes; because their vision is impure, these are called inauspicious signs.
If one uses ox-gallstone, pearl, luminous sand, honey, and powdered fine dust to stabilize the mind of the youth, one can avoid such inauspiciousness.
Ninth is walking at night and being struck by malevolent spirits. If all youths can be careful regarding these nine matters, [they will be protected].
They shall never reach death.

At that time, the heavenly Māra Pāpīyān, possessing the knowledge of others' minds, while in his palace, learned that the Buddha had preached this *dhāraṇī* mantra for longevity, the extinction of sins, and the protection of all youths.
His heart was filled with great wrath; he let out a terrible cry and was overcome with sorrow and anxiety.
He was not pleased. Māra had three daughters who came before their father king and asked, "We do not know, Great King, for what reason you are so sorrowful and distressed?
The father king replied, "The śramaṇa Gautama is currently at Vulture Peak Mountain in the great city of Rājagṛha, preaching the *Āyuṣmat-sūtra* for immeasurable and boundless sentient beings.
He is spreading [the teaching] so that all sentient beings may attain the joy of long life, thereby encroaching upon my domain."
"Kāla, an evil thought has arisen within me. I shall lead all my retinues and the entire host of Māra’s armies to go and subdue him.
Even if I cannot stop Gautama himself, by my present power I shall block the ears of all the devas and the great assembly so that they do not hear the Buddha preaching the *Āyuṣmat-sūtra*.
At that time, the three daughters of Māra admonished their father with these verses:
The celestial Māra Pāpīyān has three daughters; bowing their heads, they came before their father, the King, and said:
“The Śramaṇa Gautama, teacher of gods and men, cannot be restrained by the power of Māra.
In the past, when he first sat upon the auspicious Dharma-seat beneath the Bodhi tree, [he overcame us].”
"We three daughters are skillful, graceful, and beautiful; among all the celestial maidens, we possess a hundredfold forms that can rival the desires of the gods.
Yet the Bodhisattva has no mind of attachment at all;
he regards us three daughters as if we were old crones. Now he shall attain perfect awakening and become our Teacher."
The Father King draws his bow to strike terror, And all manner of weapons fill the void;
Yet the Bodhisattva views them as a child’s play, Without a single thought of fear or retreat.
Today you have attained the Way and become a Dharma King; I pray only that the Father King will lay aside his evil intent.
At that time, Māra Pāpīyān, having heard the verses spoken by the daughters, took his retinue and deliberated among themselves in private:

"We shall go together with you to the place where the Buddha is. By means of skillful expedients, we will feign hesitation; then, pretending to accept the Buddha's subjugation, we will cause him to place his trust in us.
Once he has gained our trust, we shall perform all manner of demonic deeds to obstruct this sutra. Thereupon, they...

Together with their retinues, they went to the place where the Buddha was, circumambulated the Buddha seven times, and addressed him, saying: "World-Honored One, are you not weary from preaching the Dharma?
We have now led our various demonic retinues here to listen to the *Dīrghāyuṣya-sūtra* and become disciples of the Buddha."
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will not go against my wish.
At that time, the World-Honored One rebuked the Māra King: "While you were in your own palace, you gave rise to a heart of anger; even if you have now come here,"
He feigned hesitation, saying, "In my Dharma, there is no room for your deception. At that time, Māra Pāpīyān was overcome with shame and humiliation;
his countenance grew pale as he composed himself and addressed the Buddha: "World-Honored One, this was my foolish scheme; I have indeed practiced deceitful methods.
I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of great compassion, will forgive my transgression. I have now heard the *Cīrṇaparivarta Sūtra* (The Scripture on Longevity) which protects all children."

Regarding this *Sutāra* dhāraṇī mantra, I make this vow: in the future final age, wherever there may be those who receive, uphold, transcribe, read, or recite this sutra, I shall provide protection for that place, ensuring that no evil spirits find an opportunity to harm them.
Even if there were a sinner in hell, should they for a mere moment bring this sutra to mind, I shall, by means of my great supernatural power, [deliver them].
They took the waters of the great ocean and poured them over the sinners, causing the great hells to become like lotus ponds.
At that time, there were also flying rākṣasas and child-eating rākṣasas, with [the former] as their leaders, who descended from the air together with their fellow kinsmen and retinues.
They circumambulated the Buddha a thousand times and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, I..."
For immeasurable kalpas, my kinsmen—who are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—have taken the form of rākṣasas.
Driven by the torment of hunger, they subsist throughout the four continents solely upon the blood and flesh of fetuses and newborn infants.
We, our retinues, wait for all sentient beings during their sexual union as husband and wife; we consume their vital essence (*śukra*) and cause them to be without conception.
Or, if they are already in the womb, we likewise enter following them, injuring the fetus and consuming its blood.

During the first seven days after birth, we specifically watch for our opportunity to sever the life-faculty (*jīvitendriya*). This continues until they reach ten years of age. We, our retinues, transform ourselves into various forms...
Various evil venomous insects enter the womb of the child and consume all the vital essence and blood within its five viscera;

they can cause the infant to vomit milk and suffer from diarrhea, or afflict it with *gaṇḍamālā* (consumptive wasting) or malaria, swelling of the eyes, dropsy, and even gradually sever the life-faculty itself.
Having now heard the World-Honored One’s preaching of the *Sūtra on Longevity, the Extinction of Sin, and the Protection of All Children*, we respectfully obey the World-Honored One’s command;
thus, even when our kinsmen are pressed by hunger, we dare not eat them.
The Buddha told the rākṣasīs, "You should receive my prohibitive precepts, so that you may cast off these rākṣasa bodies and be born in heaven to enjoy happiness.
The Buddha told the great assembly, "If there is a child who suffers from illness, let his compassionate mother divide her milk into atoms."
Together with those in the void, they bestowed [this teaching] upon all the rākṣasas.

Furthermore, by purely upholding this *Dīrghāyuṣya-pāpavināśana-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, transcribing it, and reciting it, illnesses shall be cured. At that time, the assembly of rākṣasas was filled with great joy and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"We have truly attained rebirth in heaven. We, our kinsmen, shall never again be able to invade the milk of these children. For a moment...
We shall eat iron balls rather than ever consume the blood of these youths. After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, wherever there may be those who can read,
recite, receive, and uphold this sutra, even if there are wicked people who harass such Dharma-preachers, or if there are malevolent spirits who afflict these youths,
we shall take up the Buddha’s vajra-pestle to protect them, so that no evil spirits may overcome them.
Then, at that time, all the great kings of the devas, together with their retinues, as well as all the nāga kings,
yakṣa kings, asura kings, garuḍa kings, kiṃnara kings, mahoraga kings, and pūtanas...

The many kings—the kings of the piśācas, the kings of the pūtanas, and even the khaṭvāṅga-pūtanas and all other such kings—each together with their retinues, prostrated before the Buddha, joined their palms with one mind, and spoke these words: "World-Honored One!"

From this day forward, wherever there may be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who receive, uphold, copy, or preserve this *Āyuḥpramāṇa-sūtra*, we and our retinues shall always provide protection.
We, the various kings, shall drive away malevolent spirits; if there are malevolent spirits that afflict sentient beings and cause them illness, [we shall expel them].

"Regarding those who suffer: if they can purify themselves and copy and uphold this sutra, we, the various kings, shall restrain all ghosts and spirits so that they do not inflict harm or cause them to undergo the suffering of an untimely death.
At that time, the Earth Deity Sthāvarā rose from her seat and spoke these words:
"Blessed One, if any disciple of the Buddha upholds this *Sūtra on Longevity, the Extinguishing of Sins, and the Protection of Children*, we, the earth-dwelling devas,
shall constantly bring forth the essence of the earth (*pṛthivī-rasa*) to nourish that person, causing their lifespan within the body to increase.
We shall always provide them in full with various kinds of gold and silver, various means of livelihood, and various grains."
May those with faith never lack for anything; may their bodies attain peace and stability, free from sorrow and affliction, and may their minds always be joyful.
May they obtain excellent fields of merit, and may no evil spirits sever their life-force.
If there are young children who have been born for only seven days, we, the earth deities, shall protect them and ensure that their lives are not cut short.
At that time, among the assembly, the Vajrapāṇi further addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, now that the Tathāgata has preached this *Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Longevity,
the Eradication of Sins, and the Protection of All Children*, may all the great donors and their retinues each resolve to protect,
uphold, read, recite, and transcribe this sūtra, providing all necessary supplies so that they never lack anything."
A little. I have heard, O Great Virtuous Blessed One, that you have spoken this auspicious chapter, a mantra of great spiritual power.

If there are sentient beings who hear it but once with their ears, throughout hundreds of kalpas and thousands of lifetimes, they shall never suffer a short life, but shall attain immeasurable longevity.

They shall be free from the suffering of illness. Even though the four Māras exist, they shall not be able to disturb them. Their lifespan will increase, reaching a full one hundred and twenty years, remaining neither aging nor...

Death. Without falling back or sinking, all the Buddha-sons who suffer from grievous and heavy illnesses and hear this mantra shall immediately be spared from having their lives snatched away by various ghosts. Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
Taditā (1) Cāṇḍālī (2) Cāṇḍaravite (3) Cāṇḍarama hūṃ (4) Cāṇḍaravate (5) Cāṇḍarapule (6) Cāṇḍaraśaye (7) Cāṇḍaridre (8) Cāṇḍaveye (9) Caṇṭulau (10) Cāṇḍaraparāṅga.
(11) Cāṇḍā-mudrī (12) Cāṇḍa-patye (13) Cāṇḍa-pame (14) Cāṇḍa-khage (15) Cāṇḍa-ruke (16) Subhaga. (17) The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi! You are now able to proclaim this protection for the auspiciousness of all children."
This is the Auspicious Divine Mantra. You shall become a great teacher for all sentient beings.
Mañjuśrī, you should know that this divine mantra was proclaimed by the Buddhas of the past; they established and protected it.
It is well able to increase the lifespans of humans and devas, to eliminate all defilements of sin and evil views, and to protect all who uphold this sutra, extending their [lives].
[Regarding] lifespan.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Mañjuśrī, the Son of the Dharma-King:

"After my parinirvāṇa, during the age of turbid evil, if there should be bhikṣus who violate my prohibitive precepts, who consort with bhikṣuṇīs, as well as various maidens, and the two types of śrāmaṇeras..."
Furthermore, those who drink alcohol, eat meat, and indulge excessively in sexual misconduct; who are held in contempt by laypeople; who destroy my Dharma;
who engage in worldly affairs and impure matters; who lack a sense of shame and remorse, being like mere pieces of wood—know that such individuals are people of the five heinous crimes.
They are not my disciples, but are the retinue of Māra, known as the Six Teachers. These are the bhikṣus [of such a kind].
And so forth. In this present life, they receive the retribution of a short lifespan. This is likewise true for bhikṣuṇīs and others.
If they can repent, refrain from committing such acts again, and uphold this sutra, they will immediately attain a long life.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of turbidity and evil, if there should be a bodhisattva who slanders others,
praises his own virtues, and does not transmit the Vaipulya sūtras to others— such a bodhisattva is a companion of Māra.

Such a person is not a true Bodhisattva. However, if one can with a sincere heart receive, uphold, transcribe, read, and recite this sutra, they shall immediately attain the indestructible, eternal body of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the time of the turbid and evil world, if there should be a king who kills his father or harms his mother—
They execute their own kinsmen, disregarding the royal law; they extensively raise armies and invade other nations; loyal ministers who offer remonstrance are unjustly subjected to execution;
lustful desires blaze forth, violating the laws of former kings; they destroy stupas and monasteries, and burn scriptures and images.
When floods and droughts are不调 (unregulated), it is because the king lacks the Way. Consequently, the realm suffers from famine, pestilence, and death.
Such a king shall have a short life in this world and, after death, enter hell, falling into the Great Avīci.
If one can transcribe this sutra, circulate and make offerings to it, and perform sincere repentance according to the laws of former kings, one will immediately obtain a long life.

Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of turbidity and evil, if there should be high ministers and their various officials who receive their emoluments from the state yet possess no sense of shame or remorse;
who are sycophantic and disloyal, practicing nothing but hypocrisy and deceit; such treacherous ministers who bring about harm.
The land will be unstable. Even if such persons are appointed to govern others, they will not implement the laws of the state;

instead, they will oppress and exploit the common people, acting with unrestrained greed and cruelty, executing the innocent at will, seizing the wealth and treasures of others, treating the scriptures with contempt, and creating demonic obstacles for the Mahāyāna. Such individuals as these—
In this present life, one will have a short lifespan and fall into the Avīci Hell, from which there is no time of escape.
If one can repent, receive and uphold this sutra, copy it, and recite it, one will immediately obtain a long life and forever maintain celestial fortune.

Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of turbidity and evil, there will be upāsakas and upāsikās who believe in heterodox and inverted views and do not trust the true Dharma or the Mahāyāna sūtras.

Such beings, even if they possess immeasurable hundreds or thousands of pieces of gold and silver, harbor stinginess and seek only wealth and profit; they are unable to practice giving to rescue all those in need.

Those who are impoverished and suffering cannot transcribe the twelve divisions of the sutras, nor can they receive, uphold, read, or recite them to seek liberation from the sufferings of impermanence and the evil realms.
For such people, their dwellings fall into ruin and decay; birds appear beneath their hearths, and snakes enter their sleeping chambers.
Dogs suddenly leap onto the roof; hundreds of kinds of rats screech; various wild birds and beasts vie with one another to enter the house;

and hundreds of kinds of *chima* (goblins) appear—these are called "monstrosities. Because of seeing these monstrosities, the mind gives rise to affliction (*kleśa*). Due to the accumulation of affliction, one obtains a short lifespan.
If one can receive, uphold, copy, circulate, read, and recite this sutra, one will be able to destroy such portents as these and attain long life.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of the turbid and evil world, all sentient beings— both men and women— will achieve accomplishment.

It is because of compassion that they suffer from "sickness of the heart. Why is this? When a son reaches maturity and is conscripted for military service, such being the law of the king, he is constrained against his will;

when parents think of him, it is called a sickness of the heart. Or, when a daughter reaches maturity and is married off to another family, she may be treated with contempt and fail in her duties as a wife; when parents think of her, it is called a sickness of the heart. For...
Because of the sickness of the mind, there arise grief, anxiety, suffering, and affliction; thus the sickness of grief and affliction accumulates, resulting in a short life in the present world.

If one can copy, receive, and uphold this sutra, one will obtain a long life. By the power of the sutra, one's kinsmen and relatives will become harmonious and compliant, and the sickness of the mind will be eliminated.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of turbid evil, all sentient beings will lack compassion and mercy;
they will kill living beings and take their lives, devouring the flesh from the ten parts of the bodies of all sentient beings.

Mañjuśrī, you should know that this is like killing one’s own parents or eating the flesh of one’s own six close relatives. Because of such acts as killing for the sake of life or causing injury to the fetus, in this present life—
They shall have short lifespans; even when husband and wife engage in union, they will be devoured by malevolent rākṣasas while in the womb, resulting in childlessness.
If one can copy and uphold this sutra, one will immediately be freed from this suffering.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of defilement and evil, all sentient beings will not know their past lives.
Having briefly obtained a human body, they will consider it a source of happiness; they will slander one another, or rely on their power and status, harboring various kinds of evil intentions.
Those who scheme against the lives of others, do not believe in the scriptures, and harbor arrogance toward the Mahāyāna—such persons shall have short lifespans in this present world.
If they can repent with a sincere heart, soften their minds, copy this sutra, and receive, uphold, read, and recite it, then by the power of these roots of goodness, they will attain a long life;
even if they fall ill, they shall never die an untimely death.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of turbid evil, all sentient beings—
whether by imperial decree or at the instruction of their parents— may engage in the business of trade in other lands or in perilous regions to seek various precious treasures.
For the sake of wealth and profit, they become arrogant and conceited; they engage in games of chess, *liubo*, *chupu*, and *touhu*; they associate with lewd women and evil companions;
they disregard the royal edicts and the admonitions of their parents; and through their addiction to wine and lust, they bring about the ruin of their bodies and the loss of their lives.
Even if one acquires wealth and treasures, if one is deluded and confused by alcohol, one will not know where the roads are passable or blocked.
Later, one will be plundered of that wealth by various evil bandits, who may even take one’s life.

However, if one can transcribe this sutra and extensively make vows, then wherever one is, evil bandits will retreat and disperse, giving rise to hearts of joy; no evil venomous beasts will be able to harass or harm the body.
The mind will be peaceful and secure; one will obtain abundant treasures and wealth. By the power of this sutra, one shall attain a long life.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of defilement and evil, all sentient beings, due to their evil karma, will...
Upon death, they enter hell. Emerging from hell, they take birth in the bodies of animals. Even if they obtain a human form, their six sense faculties are incomplete;

they may be deaf, blind, mute, or dumb, or suffer from physical deformities such as being hunchbacked, crippled, or afflicted with sores on the back. They receive a female body and do not recognize the characters of the scriptures. Even if they are male, [they remain deficient].
Due to their evil karma, they are deluded, ignorant, and dull-witted; they are unable to recite this *Āyuṣmat-sūtra* and their hearts give rise to sorrow and distress.
Because of this sorrow and distress, it is called a "disease of the mind. Because of this disease of the mind, they have short lifespans in the present life.
If they can cause a virtuous friend to transcribe this sūtra, and then take it up themselves to recite from beginning to end, honoring it with single-minded devotion until—
Because it is sincere, its merit is immeasurable. Such evil karma shall not be experienced again. This person will obtain a long life in the present world.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of the turbid and evil world, if there are sentient beings who, after their death—
From the first seven-day period up to the seventh seven-day period, whatever meritorious deeds and virtues are performed for the sake of the deceased,
the deceased shall receive only one-seventh of them. However, if at the time of their birth [in the next life], they can suspend household affairs during these seven seven-day periods,
copy this sutra, make offerings of incense and flowers, invite the Buddha and the Sangha, and establish the seven-day fasts, then—

One shall obtain merit equal to the sands of the Ganges River. In this present life, such a person shall attain a long lifespan and be forever freed from the sufferings of the three miserable realms and all evil paths.
If the deceased has already passed away, by establishing merit through their physical assets, they shall likewise obtain sevenfold benefits.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of turbid evil, all sentient beings will be unfilial and commit the five heinous acts;
they will lack compassion and have no sense of gratitude or affection toward their parents as they attend to their six relations.
At that time, the Heavenly King Who Practices the Path will travel around the four continents with various kinds of music, leading his retinue to the three months of fasting to reach Yama.
Jambudvīpa. If there are any sentient beings who are suddenly afflicted by various diseases, the Heavenly King Who Practices the Path shall eliminate the malevolent spirits and cause them to recover.
If sentient beings are unfilial, jealous, or commit evil deeds, the Ghost King Who Spreads Disease will immediately employ his noxious vapors.
One may suffer from ailments, contract epidemics, or any of the many grave illnesses—whether hot fevers or chills, exhaustion, chronic diarrhea, or malaria;

or be afflicted by malevolent spirits, demons, poisons, and malignant leprosy. If one can, for even a single day of the year, burn incense and scatter flowers, purify body and mind, and transcribe this sutra, or continue for up to seven days, inviting the Buddhas and welcoming the Sangha to maintain a pure fast and recite it; by means of this...
Roots of goodness. There shall ultimately be no epidemics; because there are no epidemics, they shall attain long life.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the time of the turbid and evil world when the merit of sentient beings is meager and that kalpa is about to end—
The seven suns shone simultaneously. Even if there were no seven suns, if the king lacked the Way, he would cause the heavens to suffer a scorching drought.

All that exists upon the great earth—the medicinal herbs, trees, and forests, as well as all the hundred grains, sugarcane, flowers, and fruits—was on the verge of withering and dying. If there were a king who...
For all sentient beings who are able to receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra, the Dragon King Nanda and the Dragon King Upananda,
out of compassion for sentient beings, will cause sweet rain to pour down from the waters of the great ocean upon all the groves and forests.
The hundred grains, grasses, and trees flourish and nourish all living beings; by the power of this sutra, they attain long life.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of turbid evil, all sentient beings will deceive one another with false measures and scales.
Having acquired wealth through unrighteous means, one enters hell due to those sinful karmas.
Upon emerging from hell, one receives the body of an animal—namely, an ox, donkey, elephant, horse, pig, dog, sheep, or any other beast, including mosquitoes, gadflies, lice, and ants.
If there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who, with a heart of compassion, recites this [sūtra] before such animals as well as mosquitoes and ants, [they shall be liberated].

Upon hearing this sutra but once, by the power of this sutra, all beings will understand it according to their respective kinds. These animals, after casting off these bodies, shall attain the bliss of rebirth in heaven.
If there is a bodhisattva who lacks a heart of compassion and cannot widely expound this sutra, they are not a disciple of the Buddha, but a companion of Māra.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, during the age of the five turbidities, all sentient beings will give rise to deceit and arrogance, disbelieving the sūtras and disparaging my Dharma.
Wherever there is a place where the Dharma is preached, they will have no intention to listen or study.

Because of these karmic offenses, they will have short lifespans in this present life and fall into the various hells. However, wherever this *Cīrṇabhadra-āyuṣya-sūtra* (Longevity Sūtra) is expounded—once...
All sentient beings who are able to go and listen, or who are able to exhort others, or share their seat with them— such persons are the pillars of the Buddha;
they shall attain long life and happiness, never pass through the evil realms, and propagate this Dharma of the sutra by establishing a pure altar according to the size of their room.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, after my parinirvāṇa, there will be women who carry fetuses in their wombs, who take the lives of all living beings, and who eat the eggs of various birds.
Because they lack a heart of compassion, they receive the retribution of a short life in this present world;
when the time comes for childbirth, due to the difficulties of labor, their lives may be cut short. These may be enemies rather than spiritual friends. If one can extensively make vows...
I vow that by transcribing this sutra, one shall experience an easy delivery, be free from all calamities and obstacles, and enjoy peace and happiness for both mother and child;
whether seeking a son or a daughter, they shall be born according to their wishes.

At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva: “When I now speak this *Sūtra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination of the Buddha-Nature for Longevity and the Extinction of Sin*, it is that which has been spoken together by all Buddhas of the past.

If there are sentient beings who receive, uphold, read, and recite it, they will obtain much merit and benefit. They shall live out their full lifespan to the age of one hundred and twenty; when the time comes to relinquish their life and pass away, they will not—”
Though afflicted by all sufferings, such as the "wind-blades," because of the Buddha-nature, one attains the indestructible diamond-like eternal body of the Buddhas—

tranquil, pure, and firm in every thought-moment. There are always two Bodhisattvas, the first named Avalokiteśvara and the second named Mahāsthāmaprāpta, who ride upon five-colored clouds and a six-tusked white elephant,
holding a lotus pedestal to welcome those who practice mindfulness of the Buddha, so that they are not born [into the realms of suffering].
The kingdom is in turmoil. There is natural happiness [only for those who] do not undergo the eight difficulties. Mañjuśrī, you should know:
ignorant sentient beings neither perceive nor understand that their lifespans are short and meager—like the flash of a stone struck by fire, like a bubble upon water, or like a flash of lightning.
How can they feel no alarm or fear within such a state? How can they greedily crave wealth and profit therein? How can they indulge in lust therein?
He is addicted to wine. How can he give rise to a mind of jealousy within this? In such a cycle of birth and death, one drifts upon a great ocean;
only the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas can reach the other shore, while ordinary beings will surely sink and drown. The demon of impermanence—the slayer—[is ever-present].
Its arrival knows no fixed time. Even if one possessed immeasurable and boundless gold, silver, and treasures, it would be impossible to ransom one's life through such worldly attachments.
Sentient beings should know that they must contemplate this body and give rise to this thought: "This body is like four venomous snakes."
This body is constantly being gnawed by immeasurable worms; it is foul-smelling and filthy, bound by the prison of craving and desire.
This body is loathsome, like a dead dog; it is impure, with nine orifices constantly flowing. This body is like a city with rākṣasas dwelling within. This body will not last long;
it shall soon be devoured by crows, magpies, and hungry dogs. One must abandon this defiled body.
Seeking the bodhicitta, one should contemplate this body: at the time of casting off life, white sweat flows forth and both hands are flung across the air;
the agonizing pain is unbearable. When the life-faculty is exhausted, for one day, two days, up to five days, the body becomes bloated and turns a bluish-purple hue.

Pus and sweat flow out; parents, wives, and children take no pleasure in seeing it, even until the bones of the body lie scattered upon the ground—the foot-bones in one place, the shin-bones and thigh-bones, the hip-bones, the rib-bones, the spinal vertebrae, and the skull—each in a different location.

The flesh of the body, the intestines, the stomach, the liver, the kidneys, and the lungs become a breeding ground for various worms. How could one perversely give rise [to attachment] amidst such things?
While I am alive, what concern is it to me regarding gold, silver, precious jewels, wealth, or storehouses?
If there are sentient beings who must be freed from this suffering, they should not begrudge even their kingdoms, cities, wives, children, heads, eyes, marrow, or brains;

rather, they should copy this sutra, receive and uphold it, read and recite this secret treasury of all Buddhas—the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination—and circulate and make offerings to it, moment by moment.
Accomplished. One shall attain the mind of *samyaksambodhi*, which is difficult to destroy or obstruct, and one will never meet an untimely death or be beset by violent demise.
When the Buddha preached this Dharma of the Buddha-nature of the twelve links of dependent origination amidst the great assembly, the entire multitude...
The bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, the eight classes of devas and nāgas, humans and non-humans,

and King Prasenajit along with his retinue— numbering as many as the sands of the Ganges— all attained the mind set on *samyak-saṃbodhi* and the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
They marveled at this unprecedented occurrence, prostrated themselves with single-minded devotion, and joyfully received and upheld [the teaching].
The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Dhāraṇī for Longevity, the Extinction of Sin, and the Protection of All Children.
